subject: Repeated trial/credit requests from Chainlink Labs — gating & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Potential repeated promo credit requests from Chainlink Labs

Ben —

Ops flagged a cluster of support tickets from Chainlink Labs requesting additional trial credits across four separate HubSpot contacts over the last 48 hours. Stickiness: same billing domain (chainlinklabs.com) but different contact emails and two different IP clusters that map back to overlapping ASN ranges. I've attached a quick packet (support_tickets.pdf) with ticket IDs and timestamps.

Questions: can we gate additional promo grants until fraud ops has had a look? Also worth checking if any active pilots are tracked in DL-3492.

Thanks,
Jordan
Sr. Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential repeated promo credit requests from Chainlink Labs

Jordan — good catch.

Neha / Marissa: looping you both in. Neha, can you pull the account telemetry and a quick link map (IP -> ASN -> geolocation)? Marissa, curious if you have context on whether this is a coordinated multi-team pilot (legit) or a sales tactic to get more free credits while procurement finalizes.

Immediate ask: please gate any auto-approvals for promo grants for chainlinklabs.com pending this review. If we need to escalate to Legal/Trust, tell me and I’ll make the intro.

I’ll draft a short outbound to the customer to ask for clarification on team structure so we don’t block legitimate work.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Ent. Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential repeated promo credit requests from Chainlink Labs

Quick update — I pulled the logs and attached audit_log.csv and ip_map.png. Findings so far: two distinct email clusters (teamA@chainlinklabs.com / teamB@chainlinklabs.com) but the pre-auth requests originate from three overlapping public IP ranges assigned to the same hosting provider. Several requests occurred within 12–24 minutes of each other and used the same device fingerprint string in the request headers.

This looks like coordinated retry behavior rather than independent teams. I recommend:
- Block further auto-granted promo credits to chainlinklabs.com
- Convert existing open promo requests to manual review status
- Ask the customer for an org chart and primary procurement contact if they want a consolidated pilot.

If Legal needs preserved evidence, I’ll export the full request traces.

—Neha
Trust & Safety Analyst
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <sam@chainlinklabs.com>, Akshay Malhotra <akshay@chainlinklabs.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T08:22:00Z
Subject: Quick clarification on recent trial/credit requests (Chainlink Labs)

Hi Samir / Akshay —

Thanks for using Redwood for your evaluations. We noticed several requests for additional trial credits created by different contacts at chainlinklabs.com over the last 48 hours. To make sure we handle this appropriately: can you confirm whether these were independent project teams each needing separate credits, or part of a single coordinated evaluation? Also please share the primary procurement contact for a consolidated pilot if you want us to consider a cross-team credit allocation.

We’re pausing any auto-approval of new promo grants while we confirm. If you’d like to avoid interruption, we can expedite a paid pilot quote — Marissa is copied to help with that.

Best,
Ben Carter
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Rao <sam@chainlinklabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Akshay Malhotra <akshay@chainlinklabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on recent trial/credit requests (Chainlink Labs)

Hi Ben / team —

Apologies for the noise. We are running parallel evaluations in Europe and the US (separate engineering squads) which is why you saw multiple contacts. We also had procurement turnover this week, so someone did open a couple of additional requests to keep tests running. Happy to consolidate and provide a procurement contact — attaching our internal note (support_tickets.pdf) and the contact: procurement@chainlinklabs.com.

That said, we did not intentionally script retries. If your logs show device fingerprint overlap, it’s likely internal QA tooling that spawns multiple sessions from our test harness. We can change the harness behavior and avoid additional requests.

If a paid consolidated pilot is the path forward, please share the quote.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Senior Engineering Manager | Chainlink Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential repeated promo credit requests from Chainlink Labs — decision

Team —

Summary and decision: Neha’s telemetry indicates coordinated retry behavior; Chainlink confirms parallel squads and an internal test harness that may generate duplicate sessions. Given the frequency and the risk of promo-credit exhaustion, we will:

1) Deny further auto-granted promo credits for chainlinklabs.com and move all pending promo requests to manual review.
2) Offer a consolidated paid pilot quote via Marissa (DL-3492). Marissa, please prepare a 30-day pilot quote with clear seat/usage caps and a single procurement contact.
3) Ops: add chainlinklabs.com to the watchlist for 90 days to flag repeated attempts. Neha, please preserve the exported traces in the drive folder for 12 months.

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
